title: cli-contract schema document v1
description: The machine-readable surface and fixed behavior of a CLI built with cli-contract. Apps may add their own documented facts; every other member is closed so a typo cannot pass as a fact.

schema.description: The document's id. This library writes cli-contract/cli-schema/v1; an app that renders its own document keeps its own id.

name.description: The binary name, the root of every command path.

version.description: The CLI version the --version convention reports.

cli_version.description: An app-supplied spelling of version. Either member may carry it; consumers read version first.

docs.description: A path or URL to the prose contract this document complements.

typical_flow.description: An app-supplied ordering of the commands a consumer usually drives in sequence.

envelope.description: An app-supplied description of its result envelope. The library never renders or interprets this.

commands.description: Top-level commands keyed by name. Nested commands live under their parent's subcommands.

common_flags.description: Flags registered on every command, keyed by name.

conditions.description: The inputs a consumer supplies when it evaluates the app's availability rules, keyed by condition name.

exit_codes.description: The app's named exit vocabulary. The spec fixes 0 (ok), 1 (operational), and 2 (usage); an app declares any code it adds.

signals.description: Exit codes for terminating signals, keyed by signal name. The library writes SIGINT 130 and SIGTERM 143 unless the app owns signals.

handler_owned_signals.description: The app installs its own signal handlers and chooses the exit code, so the library's signal convention does not apply.

command.description: One command's declared surface. A command that owns subcommands carries its persistent flags under flags and declares no positionals of its own.

use.description: The help synopsis. Derived from positionals; positionals is the authoritative list.

positionals.description: The positional arguments, in declaration order.

url_positional.description: The command takes exactly one required positional, the envelope contract's URL target. Derived from positionals.

no_interspersed.description: Flag parsing stops at the first positional, so later dashed tokens stay positionals.

flags.description: The command's own flags, or its persistent flags when it owns subcommands. Keyed by name.

input_rules.description: Umpire rules over this command's inputs: a rule with a field constrains one flag and is a violation only when that flag is supplied; a fieldless requires or enabledWhen rule constrains the invocation as a whole and must hold on every invocation. A duration flag's value evaluates as its canonical Go duration string, so a consumer normalizes each duration input before evaluating rules.

availability.description: Umpire rules over the document's conditions: whether a consumer offers this command at all.

kind.description: The value kind. repeat collects repeated values; integer parses base-10; duration parses a Go duration string and evaluates as its canonical Go duration string.

default.description: The value applied when the flag is absent. An integer carries a whole number, a duration its Go duration string, a duration_ms a whole number of milliseconds, and a repeat an array of strings.

required.description: The caller must supply the flag; the parser rejects an invocation without it.

output.description: How the command's stdout is decoded and which exit codes mean success. A command that declares no output mode declares nothing.

mode.description: json writes one JSON value, raw writes bytes the consumer must not decode as JSON, none writes nothing.

json_pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer to the result inside the JSON value. Only meaningful for json mode.

success_exit_codes.description: The exit codes that mean success. Required when a mode is declared: a declared block publishes exactly the codes its author stated, never a default the renderer invented.

type.description: The condition's value type, matching the Umpire v1 condition types.

description.description: What the input means, for the consumer.

field.description: The rule's subject: a tool name in availability, a flag name in input rules. Absent gates the declaring command's own tool in availability; in input rules an absent field on a requires or enabledWhen rule constrains the invocation as a whole, while disables carries no field.
